newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's disputed gold mine gets started.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's disputed gold mine gets started.

text.p: Construction of potentially the richest gold mine in Latin America started this weekend in Venezuela with ownership rights still very much in dispute.
Placer Dome of Canada put in motion the $600 million Las Cristinas gold mine project in partnership with Venezuelan state holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana (CVG).

Inaugurating the base camp Saturday at Las Claritas, southeastern Bolivar state, some 600 miles (1,000 km) from Caracas, Placer Dome's President and Chief Executive John Willson expressed confidence that the legal challenges posed by rival Crystallex International Corp would be overcome.
"We are extremely pleased that ... we are embarking on this important project in spite of the legal challenges we have experienced ... these frictions will be over soon," he said.
Crystallex has introduced a claim for the rights to Cristinas 4 and 6 concessions with the Venezuelan Supreme Court.
CVG President Elias Nadim Ynaty said he expected the result of Crystallex's appeal to come next month but he played down its importance calling the Vancouver-based firm's claim "ridiculous."
Placer, which has a 70 percent stake in Minera Las Cristinas C.A. (Minca) and CVG the rest, increased estimated reserves to 11.8 million ounces, up from nine million ounces at end-1996.

Construction of the mine is expected to take two years, Placer said in a communique. Production would start in late 1999. At capacity, Minca is set to produce 450,000 ounces of gold per year for more than 14 years "at an average cash production cost of about $200 per ounce," it said.
